items.title: Red Holloway interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: There was a school teacher, a music teacher just out of high school called Captain Walter Dyett... So he was a very, very important person in my life and a lot of other musicians’ lives. So that’s basically how I started really playing music for a living.

ctx.x: Did you have a hero? Did you have somebody on your particular instrument that you liked their sound?

Oh, yeah, Lester Young, you know. Really the first thing I started was with a clarinet because Benny Goodman and Lionel Hampton and they were working with Benny Goodman and I wanted to play clarinet which I did for a while in school, but when I heard Lester Young and the Whirleys, man, I don’t want no parts on the clarinet. I wanted to play saxophone. So basically that’s when I went — There was a school teacher, a music teacher just out of high school called Captain Walter Dyett and like Johnny Griffin went, well…
Was being in Chicago at that time, it was a big blues town, right?
